programme: ARID1A (BAF/SWI-SNF remodeling; targets SMARCA1/SMARCA2, CDH1, SMAD3, AR) and MTA3 (core subunit of the Mi-2/NuRD corepressor; targets SNAI1, CDH1, CDH2, WNT4, NCOA3) are chromatin-remodeling complexes that canonically repress the EMT transcription factor SNAI1 to hold epithelium in a differentiated, E-cadherin-positive state. BCL11B, a NuRD-interacting zinc-finger factor whose targets here are dominated by Treg/mucosal-immune genes (FOXP3, IL10, TGFB1, TGFB2, CTNNB1, NOTCH1), links that same remodeling machinery to immune tone rather than to structure alone. HES1, the canonical Notch effector, and OVOL1, a terminal-differentiation factor, sit downstream as the lineage-allocation readout of this gate (HES1 targets ASCL1, NEUROG3, NEUROD1 — the secretory-lineage program in gut epithelium; OVOL1 targets ID2, MYC, CDH2 — the EMT-suppressing differentiation program).
role_in_a: In IBS-relevant colonic epithelium, HES1/Notch signaling is the standard mechanism allocating cells between absorptive and secretory (goblet/enteroendocrine) lineages, and its dysregulation is one retrieved candidate for altered barrier/secretory function under stress (PMID 28674421 covers glucocorticoid-driven barrier dysfunction, not HES1/Notch specifically). BCL11B's Treg/IL10/TGF-β target set would, if active in gut mucosa, tune the low-grade immune activation reported in IBS, but this is not documented here.
role_in_b: In endometrial carcinoma, ARID1A is one of the most frequently disrupted tumor-suppressor genes, and its loss is independently tied in the retrieved record to altered anti-tumor immune modulation and patient stratification (PMID 40301230, 40599245, 40311467, 38876457). MTA3-type NuRD repression of SNAI1/CDH1 is the textbook mechanism by which loss of this remodeling control would permit EMT and invasion in endometrial tumors, consistent with ARID1A's established role, though no retrieved paper here places MTA3 or BCL11B in this disease.
shared_axis: If the same SWI-SNF/NuRD remodeling logic that gates epithelial differentiation and immune tone operates in both colonic and endometrial epithelium, its disruption would show up differently in each: as barrier/lineage-allocation defects and mucosal immune dysregulation in IBS, and as EMT-permissive, immune-modulated tumor growth in UCEC. This is a shared upstream mechanism producing tissue-specific downstream disease, not a shared pathology.
reasoning: The factors do assemble into a real, nameable mechanism (SWI-SNF/NuRD-gated epithelial differentiation and immune tone), and ARID1A's role in UCEC is independently well-placed by four PMIDs, so this is not incoherent. But nothing in the record connects IBS to UCEC through this axis, gut motility disorder and endometrial cancer are not an obvious anatomical or clinical pairing, and three of the five carrying factors (MTA3, BCL11B, OVOL1) have zero retrieved literature in either disease — the mechanistic link between the two diseases rests entirely on textbook complex biology, not on anything retrieved for this pair.
support: PMID 40301230 — ARID1A loss associated with anti-tumor immune modulation and survival in UCEC; PMID 40599245 — ARID1A protein expression used for UCEC patient stratification; PMID 40311467 — ARID1A among driver mutations tracked in microsatellite-unstable UCEC; PMID 38876457 — ARID1A-related pathway (KEAP1-NFE2L2) modulates prognosis in UCEC; PMID 28674421 — glucocorticoid receptor/barrier dysfunction context retrieved for HES1 in IBS, but does not test HES1 or Notch signaling directly.
how_to_falsify: In matched colonic biopsies from IBS patients vs. controls, test whether MTA3/NuRD or BCL11B/NuRD occupancy and repression of SNAI1 and Treg-gene targets (FOXP3, IL10, TGFB1/2) differ; separately, in ARID1A-mutant vs. ARID1A-wild-type UCEC lines, test whether restoring ARID1A/BAF activity reproduces the same SNAI1/CDH1 repression signature attributed to MTA3. If colonic epithelium shows no MTA3/BCL11B-dependent regulation of these targets, or if ARID1A-restored UCEC lines show a target signature unrelated to the gut findings, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Only 1 independent cohort pair underlies the 24 patient-group comparisons, so replication is limited to different clinical subgroupings of the same cohorts, not independent data sources. Tissue pairing is colorectal epithelium vs. uterine/endometrial epithelium — histologically related (both hormone- and cytokine-responsive glandular/mucosal epithelia) but clinically unconnected. No tissue-generic exclusion list was provided for this pair, so a master-regulator check against that list could not be performed; the six single-view exclusions (HDAC5, CREBRF, ZBTB2, EMX1, SIM2, MYCL) confirm the account is not riding on one idiosyncratic subgroup. TRPS1 was excluded from the programme despite 18/24 support because it was marked discordant (opposite target-set behavior between the two diseases), and its one strong UCEC citation (PMID 37344459, progesterone/RANKL) does not fit a concordant shared-programme claim. MAFB was also excluded from carrying_factors despite disease-specific evidence (PMID 42449180, IBS colonic scRNA-seq) because its known biology (macrophage/lens/pancreatic bZIP factor) does not mechanistically fit the chromatin-remodeling/EMT module described here.
